agricultural: Agricultural areas are characterized by regular geometric shapes and a patchwork pattern of cultivated fields with varying textures and colors, often indicating different crops or growth stages. Unlike tennis courts, they lack rectangular court markings and net lines; they exhibit non-uniform textures and organic boundaries compared to the structured grids of storage tanks; and they show distinct rows or plots of vegetation rather than the continuous, natural canopy of forests.
airplane: Airplanes are distinguished by their distinct fuselage and wing shapes, appearing as fixed-wing aircraft of varying sizes, often isolated or clustered on paved surfaces. Unlike runways, which are long, uniform gray strips, airplanes are discrete objects with specific structural forms; they exhibit larger scales and detailed geometries compared to the abstract road crossing patterns of overpasses; and they are not part of the regular geometric field patterns of agricultural areas.
baseballdiamond: A baseball diamond is identified by the specific arrangement of a tan or brown circular infield, white baseline lines, and a green outfield, typically situated within a larger green recreational space. Unlike golf courses, which have continuous fairways and sand traps, baseball diamonds have a fan-shaped layout; compared to mobile home parks, they lack clustered uniform rectangular roofs; and unlike general buildings, they are open sports fields rather than solid 3D structures.
beach: Beach areas are defined by smooth, bright tan or white sandy textures along coastlines, forming a clear boundary between the ocean and inland terrain. Unlike chaparral, they lack dense, woody vegetation and exhibit a uniform, untextured sandy surface; compared to rivers, beaches are static coastal landforms rather than flowing water bodies; and unlike agricultural fields, beaches are continuous shoreline strips without cultivated crop rows or geometric boundaries.
buildings: Buildings appear as individual or clustered large-scale structures with distinct rectangular footprints, varying roof colors, and often with shadows indicating verticality. Unlike dense residential areas, which are tightly packed smaller houses, these buildings are larger and less densely clustered; compared to parking lots, they are solid 3D structures rather than flat paved surfaces with rows of cars; and unlike sparse residential areas, they exhibit more complex and larger structural footprints.
chaparral: Chaparral is characterized by a continuous, rough, and mottled texture of dense, low-growing woody vegetation in natural terrain, typically appearing in muted green or brown tones. Unlike beaches, it lacks smooth sandy textures and coastal boundaries; unlike agricultural areas, it does not have regular geometric field boundaries or planted crop rows; and compared to forests, it consists of low shrubs rather than tall tree canopies, resulting in a flatter visual profile without prominent shadow patterns.
denseresidential: Dense residential areas consist of tightly packed small buildings with uniform, repetitive roof patterns, creating a high-density spatial layout. Unlike general buildings, which may be larger and more spread out, dense residential areas have smaller footprints and tighter spacing; compared to medium residential areas, the structures are closer together with less surrounding vegetation; and unlike mobile home parks, the roofs are more varied in shape and often show more complex architectural geometries.
forest: Forest areas are identified by a continuous, dense canopy of trees with a rough, mottled texture and dark green tones, often casting collective shadows. Unlike chaparral, forests feature tall trees that create a more uneven, elevated canopy surface with visible shadow patterns; compared to agricultural areas, forests lack regular geometric planting patterns and appear as natural, unstructured expanses; and unlike golf courses, they do not have manicured grass or sand traps, showing instead a wild, overgrown texture.
freeway: Freeways are wide, multi-lane linear transportation networks with smooth gray surfaces, often intersecting or crossing overpasses. Unlike intersections, which are junction points with connecting roads, freeways are long, continuous strips designed for high-speed travel; compared to runways, freeways have thinner and more complex lane configurations with medians and interchanges rather than solid, wide gray strips; and unlike agricultural areas, freeways are paved transit networks cutting through or connecting terrains rather than cultivated land.
golfcourse: Golf courses are large expanses of manicured, smooth green turf with distinct linear boundaries and water hazards, featuring patterns of fairways and putting greens. Unlike agricultural areas, golf courses have smooth, highly maintained grass textures without crop rows or harvesting patterns; compared to forests, they lack dense tree canopies and instead have open, grassy areas with isolated trees; and unlike parking lots, they are vegetated recreational spaces rather than paved surfaces with clustered vehicles.
harbor: Harbors are coastal water bodies containing numerous clustered boats and docks, often showing a mix of water surfaces and adjacent linear maritime structures. Unlike beaches, harbors are heavily modified water-land interfaces with artificial structures and vessels rather than natural sandy shores; compared to storage tanks, harbors feature elongated piers and floating objects rather than clustered cylindrical objects; and unlike airplanes, harbors contain watercraft of various shapes and sizes rather than fixed-wing aircraft on runways.
intersection: An intersection is a junction where two or more roads cross, forming a distinct cross, T-shape, or complex multi-lane interchange pattern. Unlike overpasses, which are grade-separated structures with no ground-level crossing, intersections are at-grade crossings with connecting roadways; compared to runways, intersections have thinner road widths and complex traffic patterns rather than long, wide aviation strips; and unlike parking lots, they are transit nodes rather than rectangular spaces for stationary vehicles.
mediumresidential: Medium residential areas display a mix of single-family homes with moderate spacing, showing a balance between built structures and surrounding greenery or lawns. Unlike dense residential areas, which have tightly packed roofs, medium residential areas have larger yards and more visible vegetation between houses; compared to general buildings, medium residential areas consist of smaller, uniformly shaped residential houses rather than larger commercial or industrial structures; and unlike sparse residential areas, the housing density is higher with less undeveloped land.
mobilehomepark: Mobile home parks are characterized by densely arranged, small, rectangular housing units with uniform, flat, and light-colored roofs, often aligned in rows. Unlike general buildings, which vary in size and shape, mobile home parks consist of uniform, smaller rectangular footprints; compared to dense residential areas, mobile home parks feature flatter roofs and less complex architectural details; and unlike parking lots, they are residential structures with adjacent small yards or driveways rather than purely flat paved spaces for vehicles.
overpass: Overpasses are elevated road structures that cross over other roads or terrain, appearing as distinct curved or linear bridge segments separated from the ground surface. Unlike intersections, which are at-grade junctions of multiple roads, overpasses are grade-separated crossing structures; compared to runways, overpasses are thinner linear structures with multiple lanes rather than wide, solid aviation strips; and unlike buildings, overpasses are transportation infrastructure with continuous, narrow, and elevated forms rather than distinct, clustered 3D footprints.
parkinglot: Parking lots are large, flat, paved rectangular areas with visible grid-like rows of parked vehicles, often adjacent to buildings or commercial zones. Unlike mobile home parks, which have residential structures, parking lots contain transient, smaller vehicles without attached residential footprints; compared to intersections, parking lots are stationary storage areas rather than traffic flow junctions; and unlike buildings, parking lots are flat surfaces without vertical structures, with textures defined by vehicle roofs and pavement markings.
runway: Runways are long, wide, and straight paved surfaces with distinct white or yellow edge and centerline markings, designed for aircraft operations. Unlike freeways, runways lack multiple lanes and traffic medians, appearing as single, wide aviation strips; compared to overpasses, runways are ground-level, wide, and straight rather than elevated and multi-directional; and unlike airplanes, runways are static, paved surfaces rather than discrete aircraft objects with wings and fuselages.
sparseresidential: Sparse residential areas are characterized by widely spaced individual houses surrounded by large expanses of natural or undeveloped land, showing very low housing density. Unlike medium residential areas, sparse residential areas have much larger distances between buildings and a higher ratio of natural terrain; compared to general buildings, they consist of smaller, isolated residential footprints rather than larger commercial clusters; and unlike agricultural areas, they feature built structures rather than cultivated geometric fields, though both may appear in rural settings.
storagetanks: Storage tanks are circular, cylindrical structures with smooth surfaces and distinct shadows, often grouped closely together in industrial zones. Unlike parking lots, which are flat surfaces with rectangular vehicles, storage tanks are elevated 3D structures with circular footprints; compared to buildings, storage tanks have uniform, curved geometries rather than rectangular architectural forms; and unlike baseball diamonds, they are industrial structures without sports field markings, though both may appear circular in aerial view.
tenniscourt: Tennis courts are rectangular, smooth green or blue surfaces with distinct white boundary lines and net markers, usually arranged in groups within recreational areas. Unlike baseball diamonds, which have a fan-shaped layout and dirt infields, tennis courts are strict rectangles with specific line markings; compared to parking lots, they are defined by sports surfaces rather than parked vehicles; and unlike runways, they are smaller, grouped recreational surfaces rather than long, wide aviation strips.
river: Rivers are natural, flowing water bodies with sinuous, irregular curves that adapt to the topography, often surrounded by riparian vegetation. Unlike freeways, rivers have organic, meandering boundaries rather than straight, engineered gray strips; compared to runways, rivers have irregular widths and natural textures rather than solid, uniform paved surfaces; and unlike beaches, rivers are flowing water bodies cutting through inland terrain rather than coastal sandy shores.
